read.thesis: Duke narrowed 2026 EPS to $6.70–6.80 with top-end lean, reaffirmed 5–7% growth, and is funding a $103B plan with $10B equity; supply build is large but the 15.4 GW pipeline is not yet signed.

capex.quote: we're investing about $1.5 billion a month right now, and that's going to step up to about $2 billion a month with a beginning as we get into 2027

triggers.label: Q3 load growth 2%, strongest since 2022
triggers.quote: Third quarter demand increased 2%, our strongest quarterly growth since 2022.

triggers.label: Capex run-rate $1.5B → $2B per month
triggers.quote: that's going to step up to about $2 billion a month with a beginning as we get into 2027

triggers.label: Florida tariff refiling delays large-load path
triggers.quote: We're making adjustments to our tariff and plan on refiling that.

triggers.label: 2026 EPS narrowed to $6.70–6.80
triggers.quote: we are narrowing our 2026 guidance range to $6.70 to $6.80 and expect to finish the year near the top end.

guidance.quote: we are narrowing our 2026 guidance range to $6.70 to $6.80 and expect to finish the year near the top end.
We're also reaffirming our long-term earnings per share growth rate of 5% to 7% through 2030
We remain on track to achieve our 14.5% FFO-to-debt target for 2026.
These trends reinforce confidence in our 3% to 4% load growth projection over the remainder of the 5-year plan
We remain confident in converting the full 15.4 gigawatt late-stage pipeline to ESAs by the first half of 2027.
